title: Impact of Pharmaceutical Patent Approval on Company Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study around the patent approval date (event_day = 0).
- Approach: Compute daily abnormal returns using a market model, then sum to cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) over short symmetric event windows around day 0. Aggregate CAR across firms and test whether the mean CAR differs from zero.
- Key assumptions:
  - Semi-strong market efficiency: stock prices incorporate new information quickly; abnormal returns around day 0 reflect the patent approval’s effect.
  - Correct expected return model: the provided beta is valid around the event; we use a market-model abnormal return AR_it = ret_it − (alpha_i + beta_i × mkt_ret_it). We estimate alpha_i from pre-event days (<= −6) when available; otherwise, set alpha_i = 0.
  - No confounding firm-specific information clustered at the same time across many firms; idiosyncratic news is mean zero.
  - Limited leakage: any pre-event drift is small and captured by the short event window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s61_data.csv"
df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    stock_id = as.integer(stock_id),
    event_day = as.integer(event_day),
    ret = as.numeric(ret),
    mkt_ret = as.numeric(mkt_ret),
    beta = as.numeric(beta)
  )

# Overview of available event days
rng <- range(df$event_day, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Data loaded for", n_distinct(df$stock_id), "stocks.\n")
cat("Event-day range in data:", rng[1], "to", rng[2], "\n\n")

# 2) Construct abnormal returns under three models
# (i) Market-model with firm-specific alpha estimated from pre-event days (<= -6).
# (ii) Market-model using provided beta with alpha = 0.
# (iii) Market-adjusted model (beta = 1, alpha = 0).

# Estimate firm-specific alpha from pre-event
alpha_est <- df %>%
  filter(event_day <= -6) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(
    alpha_hat = mean(ret - beta * mkt_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_pre = sum(!is.na(ret) & !is.na(mkt_ret) & !is.na(beta)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

df <- df %>%
  left_join(alpha_est, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_hat = ifelse(is.na(alpha_hat) | is.na(n_pre) | n_pre < 3, 0, alpha_hat),
    ar_mkt_alpha = ret - alpha_hat - beta * mkt_ret,  # primary
    ar_mkt_noalpha = ret - beta * mkt_ret,
    ar_mktadj = ret - mkt_ret
  )

# 3) Helper to compute CAR stats by window
compute_car_stats <- function(data, ar_col, window = c(-1, 1), min_frac = 0.6) {
  # Returns a list with mean CAR, t-stat, p-value, CI, N, trimmed mean
  win_days <- seq(window[1], window[2])
  wlen <- length(win_days)

  dd <- data %>%
    filter(event_day %in% win_days) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(
      n = sum(!is.na(.data[[ar_col]])),
      CAR = sum(.data[[ar_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(keep = n >= ceiling(wlen * min_frac)) %>%
    filter(keep)

  N <- nrow(dd)
  if (N < 2) {
    return(list(window = paste0("[", window[1], ",", window[2], "]"),
                N = N, mean = NA, se = NA, t = NA, p = NA,
                ci_low = NA, ci_high = NA, trimmed_mean = NA))
  }

  mean_car <- mean(dd$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  se_car <- sd(dd$CAR, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(N)
  t_stat <- ifelse(se_car > 0, mean_car / se_car, NA_real_)
  p_val <- ifelse(is.na(t_stat), NA_real_, 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = N - 1, lower.tail = FALSE))
  ci_range <- qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se_car
  trimmed_mean <- mean(dd$CAR, trim = 0.01)

  list(window = paste0("[", window[1], ",", window[2], "]"),
       N = N, mean = mean_car, se = se_car,
       t = t_stat, p = p_val,
       ci_low = mean_car - ci_range,
       ci_high = mean_car + ci_range,
       trimmed_mean = trimmed_mean)
}

print_car <- function(res, label) {
  cat(label, "Window", res$window, "\n",
      "  N firms:", res$N, "\n",
      "  Mean CAR:", sprintf("%.4f", res$mean), "\n",
      "  95% CI: [", sprintf("%.4f", res$ci_low), ", ", sprintf("%.4f", res$ci_high), "]\n",
      "  t-stat:", sprintf("%.2f", res$t), "  p-val:", sprintf("%.4f", res$p), "\n",
      "  Trimmed mean (1%):", sprintf("%.4f", res$trimmed_mean), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

# 4) Primary specification: market model with estimated alpha; window [-1, +1]
primary_res <- compute_car_stats(df, "ar_mkt_alpha", window = c(-1, 1))
cat("Primary result: Market model (with alpha from pre-event), CAR around patent approval\n")
print_car(primary_res, label = "Primary")

# 5) Robustness checks
# (a) Alternative event windows
alt_windows <- list(c(-2, 2), c(0, 1), c(-5, 5))
for (w in alt_windows) {
  res <- compute_car_stats(df, "ar_mkt_alpha", window = w)
  print_car(res, label = "Robustness (alt window)")
}

# (b) Alternative abnormal return models in the primary window
res_noalpha <- compute_car_stats(df, "ar_mkt_noalpha", window = c(-1, 1))
print_car(res_noalpha, label = "Robustness (market model alpha=0)")

res_mktadj <- compute_car_stats(df, "ar_mktadj", window = c(-1, 1))
print_car(res_mktadj, label = "Robustness (market-adjusted AR)")

# (c) Placebo test: pre-event window far from event (if available)
# Use window [-10, -6] if present; otherwise, the earliest 5 consecutive pre-event days
if (rng[1] <= -10) {
  placebo_window <- c(-10, -6)
} else if (rng[1] < -5) {
  placebo_window <- c(rng[1], min(-6, -1 + rng[1] + 4)) # try to get 5 days ending at -6
  if (placebo_window[2] > -6) placebo_window[2] <- -6
  if ((placebo_window[2] - placebo_window[1] + 1) < 3) placebo_window <- c(rng[1], -6)
} else {
  placebo_window <- NULL
}

if (!is.null(placebo_window) && placebo_window[1] < placebo_window[2]) {
  placebo_res <- compute_car_stats(df, "ar_mkt_alpha", window = placebo_window)
  print_car(placebo_res, label = "Placebo (pre-event)")
} else {
  cat("Placebo (pre-event) not computed: insufficient pre-event span in data.\n")
}

# 6) Also report average abnormal return by event day near the event (for diagnostics)
near_days <- seq(max(-5, rng[1]), min(5, rng[2]))
aar <- df %>%
  filter(event_day %in% near_days) %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    AAR = mean(ar_mkt_alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(event_day)

cat("\nAverage Abnormal Return (AAR) by event day (market model with alpha):\n")
print(aar, n = nrow(aar))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Patent approval should increase expected monopoly rents and reduce uncertainty, leading to a positive stock reaction.
- Magnitude: For [-1, +1], I expect a mean CAR around +1% to +3% (0.010 to 0.030), possibly larger for wider windows like [-2, +2] (+2% to +4%) if there is limited information leakage or post-announcement drift.
- Robustness: Results should remain positive and statistically significant across the alternative abnormal return models and windows; the placebo pre-event window should be near zero.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare stock returns before and after patent approval.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Patent approvals lead to a significant increase in drug-company CAR.
